figures.caption: Figure 1: Pipeline for personalized latent-dynamics modeling from scalp EEG. Non-overlapping 30-s EEG segments are encoded using our frozen EEG foundation model and mapped to shared latent-state spaces using global k-means at k=4 and k=6. Each segment is assigned a discrete state label, producing a subject-specific state sequence. The sequence is modeled independently for each subject using mLTD with group-lasso regularization across temporal lags, yielding a sparse, directed, weighted transition-dependency graph Wn ∈ Rk×k.

Table 1: Similar predictive fit, different learned structure (n=198; 99 epilepsy / 99 non-epilepsy; Mann– Whitney). Held-out CV LL measures within-subject predictive validity. En denotes the number of retained nonzero dependencies, and Dn = En/k 2 denotes the corresponding normalized dependency density. Because Dn is a constant rescaling of En within each k, separate significance tests are not reported. Mean diagonal strength summarizes self-dependency in Wn.

Figure 2: Main result overview. (A) Epilepsy minus non-epilepsy nonzero-dependency counts across k and lag. (B) Within-subject held-out CV log-likelihood at k=4 and k=6 (comparable predictive fit). (C) Group discrimination from Wn features (discussed in Section 3.2). Dashed line in (C): chance AUROC (0.5).

Figure 3: Group-mean transition-dependency matrices. Mean Wn at k=4 (top) and k=6 (bottom) for non-epilepsy (left) and epilepsy (right). Epilepsy maps are generally denser / stronger, consistent with Table 1. Latent states are unsupervised and unlabeled.

Figure 4: Between-group ROC curves from graph-derived Wn features (Section 3.2). These AUROCs measure epilepsy vs. non-epilepsy discrimination and are distinct from within-subject next-state prediction (≈ 0.86).
Table 3: Best-lag subset densification at k=4 (exploratory). E denotes mean nonzero dependencies; ∆E = epilepsy − non-epilepsy (Mann–Whitney p).

Figure 5: Lag checks at k=4. (A) Mean En among subjects with best lag = L (small subsets; exploratory). (B) Held-out CV log-likelihood vs. lag for all labeled subjects (n=198; mean±SD). Fit remains matched across groups.
